MAHALAGANG ABISO SA MGA MOTORISTA 🚦

Asahan ang mabigat na daloy ng trapiko sa mga sumusunod na kalsada sa September 7, 10, at 14, 2025, mula 2:00AM - 7:00AM at 2:00PM - 7:00PM, upang bigyang-daan ang isasagawang 2025 Bar Examinations na gaganapin sa New Era University (NEU) sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue, Quezon City:

• Commonwealth Ave. papasok ng Central Ave.
• Visayas Ave. papasok ng Central Ave.

Samantala, mananatili namang bukas ang iba pang kalsada para sa regular na daloy ng trapiko, ngunit mahigpit na ipapatupad ang NO PARKING sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue.

Mahigpit ding ipinagbabawal ang SALUBONG, PANINIGARILYO, at MAGUGULO/MAIINGAY NA AKTIBIDAD sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue.

Magtutulungan at nakaantabay ang mga tauhan ng Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD) at Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS) para maisaayos ang daloy ng trapiko sa nasabing lugar.

Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na dumaan sa mga alternatibong ruta.

Maraming salamat po sa inyong pang-unawa.

Ayon sa ulat ng Rappler, mababasa sa diyaryo ng New York Times noong Pebrero 1986 ang pagpuri ni dating US Secretary of State George Shultz sa naganap na EDSA People Power Revolution sa Pilipinas na nagpatalsik kay dating Pangulong Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr.

Batay sa article na may headline na “Shultz, Greeting New Philippine Rule, Praises ‘Peaceful Transition’,” pinuri ni Shultz ang mga Pilipino at sinabing sila ang “true heroes” dahil napatalsik nila ang diktador sa pamamagitan ng isang nonviolent protest.

Ang EDSA People Power Revolution na naganap noong Pebrero 25, 1986, 39 na taon na ang nakalipas, ay nag-ugat sa matagal na pang-aabuso sa karapatang pantao mula nang ipatupad ni Marcos Sr. ang Martial Law noong 1972 at noong pina$lang si dating Sen. Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Sr.

data.text:
ANTI-CORRUPTION GROUPS HOLD MASS AND RALLY AT EDSA SHRINE TO CONDEMN FLOOD CONTROL CORRUPTION

Tindig Pilipinas, NAGKAISA! Labor Coalition, Kalipunan ng Kilusang Masa, Simbahan at Komunidad Laban sa Katiwalian, and other pro-democracy organizations held a mass and rally on Wednesday, September 11, at the historic EDSA Shrine to denounce alleged large-scale corruption in flood control projects.

The groups said billions of pesos intended to shield Filipinos from the impact of floods were lost to ghost projects, kickbacks, and collusion between politicians and contractors. They described the scandal as another betrayal of the Filipino people, particularly the poor and vulnerable who suffer the most during floods and climate disasters.

"We cannot stay silent while our money is being stolen, while our people drown in both floods and corruption," said Kiko Aquino Dee, convenor of Tindig Pilipinas.

"Every peso pocketed by these corrupt officials is a classroom not built, a health center left unfinished, and flood protection denied to our communities. That is why we demand: buuin na ang isang independent commission to investigate this massive corruption, and release the SALNs of all public officials involved. Transparency and accountability must begin now," he added.

Judy Ann Chan Miranda of the NAGKAISA! Labor Coalition said the issue was a matter of moral urgency. "This is not just about corruption, it is about life and death, justice and injustice. The billions stolen from flood control projects could have saved lives and livelihoods. We gather at EDSA Shrine because we believe that, once again, the Filipino people must rise to demand truth, accountability, and reform."

The coalition stressed that the EDSA Shrine—long a symbol of people power against tyranny and abuse—was the rightful venue for Filipinos to declare their stand.

"Our call is simple: end corruption, hold the thieves accountable, and return the money to the people. Gawin nating kadiri muli ang kurapsyon," Dee said.

#MSNews | Retired Supreme Court Senior Associate Justice Antonio Carpio on Saturday urged the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to educate the public the legal and historical foundations of the country's sovereignty over Bajo de Masinloc.

"China’s declaration raises the issue of what state has sovereignty over Bajo de Masinloc – the Philippines or China. Thus, it is not enough for the [DFA] to lodge a perfunctory protest against China. The DFA must explain to the Filipino people and the world the legal and historical bases of Philippine sovereignty over Bajo de Masinloc," he said in a statement.

Carpio opined that China's declaration of a “national nature reserve” at Bajo de Masinloc violates the country's sovereignty as it is Philippine territory under local laws. | via Pot Chavez
